title: Gaussian isoperimetric bound from averaged profiles
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $0<\alpha<1$. If, for every $u\in(0,\pi/2)$, the extended nonnegative value of the closed Gaussian profile at $\alpha$ is at most the extended nonnegative value of its integral over the averaged Gaussian indicator of $A$ at angle $u$, plus the Gaussian surface area of $A$, then the extended nonnegative value of the Gaussian isoperimetric profile at $\alpha$ is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $u\in(0,\pi/2)$, the extended nonnegative profile bound holds
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, $0<\alpha<1$, and let $U$ be the standard Gaussian isoperimetric profile extended by zero outside $(0,1)$. Set $f_u(x)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,G)]$. If $U(\alpha)\le[\int U(f_u)\,d\gamma_n]_++P_\gamma(A)$ for every $0<u<\pi/2$, then $U(\alpha)\le P_\gamma(A)$.
